Read reproducibility data embedded in a PNG

Source: R/embed.R
read_ggsaveR_data.Rd

Extracts the information that ggsave() embeds in a PNG file when the ggsaveR.embed_data option is TRUE.

Usage

read_ggsaveR_data(path, trusted = FALSE)

Arguments

path

Path to a PNG file written by ggsave().

trusted

If TRUE, also restore the serialized plot object. Files written by ggsaveR 0.1.0, which stored everything as one serialized object, can only be read with trusted = TRUE.

Value

A list with some or all of these elements, depending on the ggsaveR.embed_metadata option in effect when the file was saved:

ggsaveR_version

Version of ggsaveR that wrote the file.

plot_call

The expression passed as plot, as a string.

session_info

The printed sessionInfo(), as a string.

plot_data

The plot data as a data frame, read back from CSV. Column types are those utils::read.csv() infers; factor levels, dates and row names are not kept. Use plot_object$data for the exact data.

plot_object

The plot object, only with trusted = TRUE.

Returns NULL, with a warning, if the file holds no ggsaveR data or cannot be read.

Security

The plot object is stored as a serialized R object. Restoring it with unserialize() can run arbitrary code, so it is only read when you set trusted = TRUE. Do that only for files that you, or someone you trust, created. The call, session information and data are stored as plain text and CSV, and are always safe to read.

Reading the data outside R

The data are stored in the PNG text chunk ggsaveR_data_csv as a UTF-8 CSV file, compressed with zlib and base64 encoded. In Python, for example: zlib.decompress(base64.b64decode(text)). The call and session are in the plain-text chunks ggsaveR_call and ggsaveR_session, which tools such as exiftool show directly.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) + geom_point()
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "embedded.png")

old <- ggsaveR_options(embed_data = TRUE)
ggsave(out, p, width = 5, height = 4)
#> Embedded reproducibility data into embedded.png (304.6 Kb)
options(old)

info <- read_ggsaveR_data(out)
#> 'embedded.png' also holds the plot object. Use `trusted = TRUE` to restore it, but only if you trust the file.
info$plot_call
#> [1] "p"
head(info$plot_data)
#>    mpg cyl disp  hp drat    wt  qsec vs am gear carb
#> 1 21.0   6  160 110 3.90 2.620 16.46  0  1    4    4
#> 2 21.0   6  160 110 3.90 2.875 17.02  0  1    4    4
#> 3 22.8   4  108  93 3.85 2.320 18.61  1  1    4    1
#> 4 21.4   6  258 110 3.08 3.215 19.44  1  0    3    1
#> 5 18.7   8  360 175 3.15 3.440 17.02  0  0    3    2
#> 6 18.1   6  225 105 2.76 3.460 20.22  1  0    3    1

# The plot object itself: only for files you trust
restored <- read_ggsaveR_data(out, trusted = TRUE)$plot_object
